card.name: Cakalele
card.era: Pre-colonial; tied to historic Moluccan warrior raids
card.tagline: Moluccan war dance of dueling captains and shields
card.profile: Cakalele (spelled tjakalele by the Dutch) is a war dance from the Maluku Islands of Indonesia (Wikipedia). It is performed by men, two of whom represent opposing captains while others are supporting warriors; after an opening ritual the captains engage in a mock duel with a spear (sanokat) and a long parang (lopu), while supporters carry a parang and a long shield (salawaku). Dancers wear full warrior costume and move to the rhythm of the tifa drum, gong and suling (fife). The dance originated as a way for warriors to celebrate after a successful raid and survives today as a welcoming and ceremonial dance honoring ancestors.
card.insight: Hybrid versions of cakalele spread across eastern Indonesia, giving rise to related war dances such as the Minahasan Kabasaran of North Sulawesi (Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: Maluku war dance with parang & shield. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Maluku, Indonesia.
